dedupe_keys.name: enhancing 5g network slicing slice isolation via actor critic reinforcement learning with optimal graph features

description: SIRL uses actor-critic reinforcement learning and five graph features to allocate network slices while maintaining isolation. A ranking scheme reduces feature dimensionality. The authors compare nine reinforcement-learning baselines using four metrics and report average 70 percent higher request coverage and 8 percent lower attack-related damage. These are study-relative results, not absolute service guarantees or reproduced measurements. The model is documented through a publication; executable code, benchmark traces, complete feature definitions and uncertainty intervals are not established in inspected metadata. Transferability to different traffic and threat conditions remains unknown. The source authors provide the native description and file descriptors through Zenodo. Only metadata was inspected, without reading measurements, archives, source code or document bodies.
